answer.evidence: Rows 1-5 form a top band: a dark row 1, then lighter brown rows 2-4, ending in a lighter front-edge line at row 5 (L=157). Rows 6-7 below it are black eave shadow. The front face runs from row 6 to row 31, about 26 rows, with three open shelves holding cheese wedges. The shelf lips at rows 12-13, 21-22 and 29-30 are thin rims, not top surfaces. The structure matches the green 'cabinet: top 5 + edge + eave' reference. No receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small shelf cabinet with cheese wheels, about 14x32 source pixels. It has 13 distinct colours in total. The comparable solid props, the cheese stall and the roofed well, have 38-40 colours, and their tiles carry 17-20 colours against the candidate's 13. The candidate has no flat 5x5 fills, which is good. Its dark edge pixels are 68% near-neutral, so the outline leans toward a near-black sticker line rather than the tinted dark-brown wood tone of the stall and hedge (0-1% neutral). The wood frame and shelves show only about 3-4 lightness steps, and the cheeses are 2-3 tones with little per-item shading or grain. It is clean and readable but shallower in shading and outline craft than the stall and well references, so it fails when in doubt.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small one-tile-wide cabinet with shelves of cheese wheels. It has 13 colours in total and a median of 13 per 16x16 tile. That is on par with the small references (hedge 10, bench 14, lamp 14) and well under the larger ones (stall-cheese 40, well 38). There are no flat 5x5 fills (0%). The wood frame and the cheese wheels each show only about 3-4 lightness steps, against about 5-6 on the references. The cheeses have little per-wheel highlight or grain, and the cabinet has no scalloped or speckled detail like the stall's awning and counter. Of its dark edge pixels, 68% are near-neutral, which is higher than the accepted bench (44%) and the stall (1%) and points to a fairly uniform dark outline, not one tinted to each adjoining material. That makes the outline mixed, leaning toward the sticker look. The cabinet is clean and readable, but it is shallower and more outlined than the references. Given the instruction to fail when in doubt, it fails.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small wooden shelf holding cheese wedges. It has 13 distinct colours in total, against 38-40 for the comparable stall and well references. Its 13 colours per tile do beat the hedge (10) and sit just under the stall (17), so tile density alone is acceptable. The wood frame reads as only about 3 steps (a light plank, a mid tone and a dark edge), and the cheese as about 2-3. The references carry 5-6 steps per material. 68% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the dark frame outline leans neutral black rather than a tinted dark brown. The stall and hedge references are almost entirely tinted (1% and 0% neutral), and the well sits at 33%. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, and the shelf boards and cheese have some dot variation, but the shading is shallow and the outline has the sticker look. A careful artist would not accept it beside the stall reference without more ramp depth and a tinted outline.
